approach: Add one reading check, `check_records_measure`, in `crates/athena-core/src/reading/surveys.rs` beside `check_history_fixture`, with the same gate (`changes_code_with_behavior_criterion`, surveys.rs:237 area). It scans the summary and each criterion for a records-computed measure (throughput, keep rule, planning cost, refusal rate(s), check duration(s), landing time(s)) as whole words on lowercase, whitespace-normalised text with hyphens and underscores read as spaces. A criterion that declares the replay share (it contains `newly refused`, e.g. `expected N% of newly refused readings`) is skipped, and the sentence `higher refusal rate is intended` is also removed after whitespace normalisation, so a wrapped declaration passes. A reading that names a measure is accepted only if one Behavior criterion names `real records`, an independent source (`git log`, `history.json`, `commit times`, `recorded check durations`, `recorded durations`) and `expected range`. Otherwise it bails, naming the measure and the missing parts. A code reading that only says a measure is unchanged is refused on purpose (the lexical check cannot tell, and the fix is one criterion); the doc comment states this limit. The step goes in as one `step!` line in `refusing_check` (checks.rs:518), right after `check_history_fixture` (checks.rs:538). The reader line and planner line go where the brief text is built (`READING_RULES` in briefs/reader.rs:287, a new `REAL_RECORDS_RULE` in briefs/planner.rs interpolated into the Report string at planner.rs:134). The reader section limit stays `< 3150`: existing rule lines are shortened by at least the new line's length, so the section does not grow, and the measured size goes in the test comment. The planner test bounds growth to the rule's length plus 4 bytes.

decisions.choice: Keep the four files outside the reading's deliverable list (checks.rs, refusal_corpus.rs, briefs/reader.rs, briefs/planner.rs) and say why in the plan. Answers findings 1-4. checks.rs holds `refusing_check` (checks.rs:518) and its `step!` macro (checks.rs:525), so the chain line cannot go in reading.rs or surveys.rs. refusal_corpus.rs must gain a refusing case for the new step line, because `every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case` (refusal_corpus.rs:2733) fails otherwise, and the planner brief requires the corpus for any new reading check. briefs.rs only declares `mod planner; mod reader;` and holds tests; the rule text is built in reader.rs:287 and planner.rs:134.
decisions.reason: Each is the single place the behavior lives, found by reading the code. Nothing else outside the deliverables is touched.

rejected.option: Call `check_records_measure` from inside `check_history_fixture` so checks.rs is untouched
rejected.why: It hides a second rule in a function named for another, the corpus step extractor (refusal_corpus.rs:2704) would not see it as its own check, and `history_fixture_has_one_step_line` would be confused.

rejected.option: Skip the corpus cases to stay inside the deliverables
rejected.why: `every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case` would fail and `cargo test` with it.

rejected.option: Put the brief lines in briefs.rs
rejected.why: They would not reach the generated briefs, so the brief tests would not see them.

decisions.choice: Do not raise the reader section limit. Keep `assert!(section.len() < 3150)` (briefs.rs:3558). Write the new reader line to the criterion-1 wording (a records-computed measure change needs a criterion run on real records with an expected range from an independent source, naming `check_records_measure`), at most 220 characters including the leading `- `. Shorten existing `READING_RULES` lines (prose-only Test placement, Previous result, Governance files, Design, Valid reading) by at least the new line's length plus 3 bytes, keeping every phrase the tests pin (`Consumers:`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `Term ladder:`, `Environment:`, `Existing code:`, `(prose only).` endings, each check name). Before editing, the producer prints the baseline `section.len()` once (a temporary failing assert), then records the baseline and the new size in the test comment and asserts the section is no longer than the baseline. Answers finding 5.
decisions.reason: The brief's acceptance says the briefs stay within their size limits, and the accepted reading says the reader line must replace or shorten existing wording. The test comment gives about 3045 of 3150 (briefs.rs:3555-3558), so only about 100 bytes are free. The new line is longer than that, so wording must shrink elsewhere.

rejected.option: Raise the limit to the new measured size plus a margin (the round 1 plan)
rejected.why: It makes the size test pass without meeting the criterion.
Many tests pin its phrases (briefs.rs:3562 onward) and it carries the refusal-rule guidance this check relies on.

decisions.choice: State a fixed planner bound. `REAL_RECORDS_RULE` is a single line of at most 200 bytes. The new planner test finds it exactly once in the Report section, and asserts `report.len() <= REPORT_BASE + REAL_RECORDS_RULE.len() + 4`, where REPORT_BASE is the Report section length measured with empty inputs before the change and written in the test as a constant. Answers finding 6.
decisions.reason: Later growth of the Report section fails the test. 200 bytes is about 67 tokens, under the reading's 95 tokens of planner headroom (1105 of 1200, docs/system-facts.md), so the line fits even if the planner budget is counted.

rejected.option: No bound, as in round 1 ('grows by less than a stated number of bytes')
rejected.why: No number was given, so nothing would fail.

decisions.choice: Handle refusal-rate declarations structurally. A criterion whose normalised text contains `newly refused` (the replay-declaration form that `declared_percent`/`replay_declaration` recognise, replay.rs:227 and replay.rs:263) is not scanned. In other criteria and the summary, the sentence `higher refusal rate is intended` is removed after the text is lowercased and whitespace-normalised (split_whitespace joined by single spaces, as `normalised` at replay.rs:216 does), so a sentence wrapped across a line (reading.rs:5365-5367) is still removed. A new test covers the wrapped form. Answers finding 7.
decisions.reason: The reader brief tells readers to write that declaration for every refusal rule (briefs/reader.rs:311-312). A declaration must not trip a different rule. The structural skip does not depend on one exact sentence. The sentence strip covers a declaration without a percent.

rejected.option: Remove only the literal sentence from raw text
rejected.why: A wrapped sentence escapes it, and other wordings with `expected N%` would be refused.

rejected.option: Drop `refusal rate` from the measure list
rejected.why: The request names refusal rates as a measure.

decisions.choice: Accept these independent sources: `git log`, `history.json`, `commit times`, `recorded check durations`, `recorded durations`. The refusal text says the verifier reads `history.json` commit times and `landings/` from the evidence snapshot (evidence_section, briefs.rs:651-668; `status --snapshot <path>` prints the throughput section), which needs no `Environment:` assumption, while `git log` is in ENV_LOCATED_SOURCES (surveys.rs:561-567) and needs one. Answers finding 8.
decisions.reason: The verifier has no git repository, only the snapshot. A reader who follows the hint should not hit `check_environment_reach` next, because the reader gets one second read.

rejected.option: Accept only `git log` and recorded check durations
rejected.why: The verifier cannot run `git log` on the records snapshot, and `git log` forces an extra Environment assumption.

decisions.choice: Refuse a code reading that names a measure only to say it is unchanged, and add a corpus case `records-measure-named-as-unchanged` that expects Refuse. The doc comment's limits say so, and the refusal text says to add the real-records criterion. Answers finding 9.
decisions.reason: The check is lexical and cannot read negation, as `check_history_fixture` states (surveys.rs:320-321). A change near a measure can still move it, which is how both 2026-10-29 landing-time figures went wrong. The cost is one criterion. HISTORY.txt subjects naming these measures: lines 441, 709, 1233, 1266, 1285 and 1400, 6 of 200 commits, which supports declaring 3%. The replay at verification measures the real share, and a share above 3 plus 5 points holds the job.

rejected.why: It needs negation parsing and opens the exact gap that produced the wrong figures.

decisions.choice: Match measures only in the summary and criteria, not in deliverable paths.
decisions.reason: The gate and helpers (`has_phrase` surveys.rs:39, `straight_lowercase` surveys.rs:286) exist and cost no model call. A path trigger would flag every edit to a file such as status.rs.

rejected.option: Also trigger on paths such as status/throughput.rs
rejected.why: It flags refactors that change no figure and needs its own corpus forms.
It adds a model call and is not reproducible.

decisions.choice: Satisfy the rule only with one Behavior criterion that holds `real records`, an independent source and `expected range`.
decisions.reason: A single criterion ties the real run to the independent range. A Content criterion does not run anything, and the failures in the request were fixture runs.

rejected.option: Accept the parts spread across several criteria
rejected.why: A real-records criterion could then have no range.
It needs a number parser and more corpus forms; the lexical phrase matches `check_history_fixture`.

risks.risk: Criterion 1 says the added lines are in briefs.rs, but the text is built in briefs/reader.rs and briefs/planner.rs; briefs.rs holds the tests (briefs.rs:17-18, 3493).
risks.mitigation: The criterion-1 demonstration diffs the two sub-module files, where there is one added rule line each; the plan lists all three files.

risks.risk: Shortening existing reader rule lines to keep the section under 3150 could break a test that pins their wording, or lose meaning.
risks.mitigation: The producer keeps every pinned phrase (Consumers:, CHANGELOG.md, Term ladder:, Environment:, Existing code:, check names, (prose only) endings), trims only filler words, and runs `cargo test -p athena-context`. If the section cannot fit without losing a rule, the producer stops and reports instead of raising the limit.

risks.risk: False positives: a code reading that mentions a measure word only in passing, or only as unchanged, is refused.
risks.mitigation: The gate needs a capability, no question, class code or tests and a Behavior criterion. Declaration criteria and the 'higher refusal rate is intended' sentence are exempt. The refusal text gives an example criterion. The corpus pins the unchanged case as Refuse and the doc comment says so. The declared 3% is an estimate; the replay at verification measures the share, and a share above 3 plus 5 points holds the job.

risks.risk: The check is lexical: a criterion can hold the three phrases without running anything on real records, and a measure can be named in unlisted words such as merge latency.
risks.mitigation: The doc comment states the limits. The check makes sure the criterion exists; the verifier runs it against the evidence snapshot (evidence_section, briefs.rs:651-668). Making the verifier fetch records is out of scope.

risks.risk: A reader who satisfies the rule with `git log` then meets `check_environment_reach` and has one second read.
risks.mitigation: The refusal text points to `history.json` commit times from the evidence snapshot, which need no Environment assumption, and says `git log` needs one. Tests cover both forms through the whole chain.

risks.risk: The planner could not run the tests, so the baseline sizes (reader section about 3045, REPORT_BASE) are not measured here.
risks.mitigation: The producer measures both before editing, records them in test comments, and the tests assert against the measured values. The plan cites no result it did not see.
